title: Editorial Commentary: Elbow Injury Results When Pediatric and Adolescent Throwing Athletes Throw as Hard as Possible, and Weighted Baseball Training Should Be Banned for Youth Athletes.
journal: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association

sections.label: UNLABELED
sections.text: We are in the middle of an epidemic involving pediatric and adolescent throwing athletes. Too many young athletes have elbow injuries, and it is unnerving how young surgical indications can present. Increased competition has led to increased demands before athletes have reached their full adult size. Evidence shows that higher ball velocity, higher shoulder external rotation angle, and higher arm speed are associated with increased medial elbow torque and elbow injury in this population. Pediatric and adolescent athletes should not try to throw as hard as possible, and weighted baseball training should be banned for youth athletes.
